nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Economic analysis_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What was Georgescu-Roegen's contribution to the concept of bioeconomics?
nodes.answer: Georgescu-Roegen used the concept of bioeconomics to emphasize the need for a new form of economic analysis that accounts for the biophysical roots of economic processes and addresses the sustainability issues resulting from industrialized societies' use of natural resources.
nodes.paragraph: Georgescu-Roegen S use of the concept bioeconomics represented an urgent call for a new form of economic analysis capable of addressing the implications of the biophysical roots of the economic process and the incompatibility between the use of natural resources by industrialized societies and the regeneration processes of ecological systems (i.e., the lack of sustainabil- ity) already emerging at his time (Mayumi 2001). Thus, in its original interpretation, bioeconomy i.e., the interaction of the economic process with the embedding ecosystems required a new discipline, bioeconomics, complementing conventional economics, to provide a holistic view of the factors determining sustainability (Gowdy and Mesner 1998; Mayumi 2001). The second interpretation of the term bioeconomy surfaced during the late nineties and was about a strategy of technical innovation based on the limitation of biological and ecological processes (i.e., biomimicry or nature-inspired innovation) (Vivien et al. 2019). This interpretation supports the belief that major improvements in the efficiency and sustainability of the economic process can be achieved by technological innovations using nature as a mentor . Also called the knowledge-based bioeconomy, it was expected to facilitate the development of a bio-based economy powered by industrial biotechnology, which was essential to deliver on post-Paris (COP 21) climate commitments, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and the dependence on fossil resources (Patermann and Aguilar 2018).

nodes.question: What is highlighted in the critical analysis regarding the use of economic growth?
nodes.answer: The critical analysis highlights the importance of implementing expenses for alternative energies that can reduce polluting emissions based on the qualitative approach of economic growth.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract The aim of this study is to explore the nexus among CO 2emissions, energy use, and GDP in Russia using annual data ranging from 1970 to 2017. We rst conduct time-seriesanalyses (stationarity, structural breaks, and cointegration tests). Then, we present a newD2C algorithm, and we run a Machine Learning experiment. Comparing the results of thetwo approaches, we conclude that economic growth causes energy use and CO 2emissions. However, the critical analysis underlines how the variance decomposition justi es the quali-tative approach of using economic growth to immediately implement expenses for the use ofalternative energies able to reduce polluting emissions. Finally, robustness checks to validatethe results through a new D2C algorithm are performed. In essence, we demonstrate theexistence of causal links in sub-permanent states among these variables. Keywords CO 2emissions Energy use Economic growth Machine learning D2C algorithm Time-series Russia JEL Classi cation B22 C32 N55 Q43 1 Introduction Economic growth affects the way a country uses energy and in return is likely to increase the rate of carbon dioxide (CO 2) emissions in the atmosphere. It comes as a result of development and increases in industries, which consume more and more energy (Malik & Lan, 2016 ).

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How do the explanatory powers of selected economic variables compare to common economic factors?
nodes.answer: The explanatory power of selected economic variables is larger than that of common economic factors when extracted using the 2SKF procedure.
nodes.paragraph: In this paper, we analyse the short-run relationship between economic activity and CO 2emissions in Spain, by tting a SADFM to annual rates of growth of Spanish CO 2 emissions with the factors extracted by 2SKF from a large set of Spanish macroeco-nomic variables. 2SKF is an unsupervised factor extraction procedure, which combinesinformation contained in all macroeconomic variables independently from the target variable. Additionally, we also consider factor extraction orientated towards pre- diction of the rate of growth of CO 2emissions. In particular, we extract factors using partial least squares (PLS) as proposed by Wold ( 1966 ). We conclude that the explana- tory power of selected economic variables is larger than that of common economic factors when the latter are extracted using the 2SKF procedure. However, the pre-dictive power of the common factors increases when they are extracted using PLS. We nd that the PLS common factors recover some explanatory power for explaining CO 2emissions beyond the information content of the selected individual economic indicators. Our results somehow differ from those found by Bennedsen et al. ( 2021 ) for the US economy as the outstanding predictors for CO 2emissions in Spain are private consumption and maritime transport of merchandise, while theirs rely more on IP .

nodes.question: Which macroeconomic method does Fosten (2019) use to represent economic activity in his analysis?
nodes.answer: Fosten (2019) uses a single factor extracted using Principal Components (PC) from a set of macroeconomic variables to represent economic activity.
nodes.paragraph: There is a wide agreement about the link of CO 2emissions and economic activity; see, for example, Dong et al. ( 2020 ) and Economic activity and CO 2emissions in Spain 1381 is analysed by Esteve and Tamarit ( 2012a ,b), Sephton and Mann ( 2013 ), Balaguer and Cantavella ( 2016 ), and Moutinho et al. ( 2017 ), among others. In general, models tting the EKC show very diverse evidence. Alternatively, Fosten ( 2019 ) focuses away from the long-run EKC and analyses the short-to-medium run impact of economic activity on CO 2emissions. In the context of the US, Fosten ( 2019 ) proposes a factor-augmented regression model to repre- sent short-to-medium run relationship between seasonally-adjusted monthly growth r a e so ft o t a IC O 2emissions and economic activity, which is represented by a single factor extracted using Principal Components (PC) from a set of macroeconomic vari-ables. He concludes that emissions are not linked to economic activity in the short-run (one month) but nds strong linkages when looking at cycles uncovered at time- scales of length one to three years.
